19 A metal wire, fixed at one end, has length l and cross-sectional area A. The wire extends a
distance e when mass m is hung from the other end of the wire.
What is an expression for the Young Modulus E of the metal?
ml
B
E = mgl
Ae
C
E = me
Al
D
E = mge
Al
A
E = Ae

hints: Notice the load is a mass $m$ hung on the wire, so the tensile force $F$ stretching the wire is its weight $mg$, not $m$.
Recall Young modulus is $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$ with stress $= F/A$ and strain $= e/l$ for area $A$, length $l$ and extension $e$.
Combine as $E = (F/A)/(e/l) = Fl/Ae$ and then substitute $F = mg$ to select the matching expression.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: original length $l$, area $A$, extension $e$, and stretching force equal to the weight of mass $m$, so $F = mg$.
State the governing rule: $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$, where stress $= F/A$ and strain $= e/l$.
Replace $F$ with $mg$ to get $E = mgl/Ae$ with unit $\text{Pa}$, matching stress over dimensionless strain.

A.explanation: This uses $m$ instead of weight $mg$ for the tensile force, so the units are not those of pressure and the force is too small by factor $g$.

C.explanation: This inverts extension $e$ and original length $l$ and omits $g$, giving strain as $l/e$ instead of $e/l$.

D.explanation: This correctly uses weight $mg$ but inverts $e$ and $l$, so it is proportional to $e/l$ inverted.
